hook_text: Tut, pop, click: why does isiXhosa have these sounds?
clip_script: Qonce, an isiXhosa lesson. C, Q, X: three click sounds. Many of them came from Khoisan languages, long ago. When the first farmers settled in the east, the San and Khoikhoi already lived there. Farmers often welcomed strangers with food, shelter and land. The groups traded skins and honey for grain and iron, worked together, and married. Many Khoisan became part of farming communities. Their clicks live on in our languages today.
visual_style: Whiteboard letters c, q and x with sound waves popping out, then two groups trading and joining hands around a village.
mood: Warm and surprising, like discovering a family secret.
pacing: Playful clicks to start, then a gentle story of meeting, trading and joining.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and practise the three isiXhosa clicks with a friend.
